newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, PLO meet on resuming peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Israel, PLO meet on resuming peace talks.

text.p: Israel's defence minister and a senior PLO official met on Wednesday under U.S. and Egyptian auspices to try to revive formal peace talks, diplomatic sources said.
At a NATO summit in Madrid, U.S. President Bill Clinton said he was very concerned about the deadlock in the Middle East peace process and was working on new ideas to get it moving again.
"It is obvious that we're going to have to see some new specific actions taken in order to get this thing going again," Clinton told a news conference.
"I'm very concerned about what's happening in the peace process. I'm very concerned about the growing tensions between the Palestinians and the Israelis," Clinton said.
Formal Israeli-PLO peace talks have been frozen since the government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu began building a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March.

The meeting on Wednesday, scheduled before Clinton made the remarks in Madrid, was aimed at finding "a common ground and a way to restore negotiations to their correct path," said a spokesman for Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.

Diplomatic sources said Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai, Palestinian Minister of Planning and International Cooperation Nabil Shaath, U.S. Ambassador to Israel Martin Indyk and Egyptian Ambassador Mohammad Bassiouny took part.
They had planned to convene at Indyk's residence but Israel Radio said the meeting was held at Bassiouny's home near Tel Aviv instead after news of the location leaked to the press.
"This is part of ongoing meetings...to implement interim agreements," one diplomatic source, who is close to the negotiations, said about Wednesday's talks.

PLO officials said the meeting would focus on confidence- building measures, including operating a Palestinian airport in Gaza, building a seaport and a three-stage Israeli pullback from rural areas in the West Bank, agreed under interim peace deals.

Netanyahu has proposed moving straight into negotiations on a final peace settlement with the Palestinians rather than pursuing crisis-plagued talks on implementing outstanding elements of interim deals signed since 1993.

"I believe that contrary to all the detractors and depressing prophecies, our government...can achieve a permanent peace agreement with the Palestinians, on condition they want one," Netanyahu told Israel's Channel One television.

The PLO demands he first halt the settlement-building at Jabal Abu Ghneim, or Har Homa, on Israeli-occupied land in East Jerusalem before full-fledged talks can resume. Netanyahu has pledged repeatedly to press ahead with the construction.
The PLO has also been cool to Netanyahu's proposal to move into "final-status" talks before implementing the rural redeployment in the West Bank.
Egypt has tried in recent months, with little apparent success, to mediate between the two sides after U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross failed to break the deadlock.

In another sign of Israeli-Palestinian tensions, shots were fired on Wednesday at a building housing Jewish settlers in the divided West Bank town of Hebron, the scene of recent street battles between Arab stone-throwers and Israeli troops.
Witnesses and Israeli military sources said no one was hurt but at least one bullet hit an outer wall of the Beit Hadassah settler enclave.
